# M7 · W4 — the corpus generator: walks rendered by the runtime, values nobody can memorise (pre-registered 2026-09-19)

**Question.** Can a training corpus for the navigation habit be *generated by driving the W2 runtime*
— every observation written by `memory/runtime.py`, never imitated — such that nothing a note supplies
can be memorised, the procedure W5 will score was never walked, and every row is a walk the referee
itself accepts? No model runs; this is a gate over a generator.

**Why now.** W5 is the arm that can kill the memory, and it is only as good as its corpus: a fixed
14-value table was memorised by a control with no lookup tool, 27/30 **[ran]** P15, P21; a copy of a
renderer drifted into 71 refused calls **[ran]** P38; a corpus with one depth taught a floor **[ran]**
P45; a specialist is confidently wrong one step outside its region, 1/20 **[ran]** P14.

**The gate — written before the generator exists, persisted as `gate.json`.** For corpus $C$,
evaluation sets $E$, held-out-only notes $H$, and per row $r$ the values $V(r)$ its walk obtains from a
note's slots or from `<calc>`, the givens $G(r)$ its statement must state, and the numbers $N(r)$ in
its statement:

$$\text{pass} \iff \forall r \in C \cup E:\; V(r) \cap \big(N(r) \setminus G(r)\big) = \varnothing \;\wedge\; V(r) \cap G(r) = \varnothing$$
$$\wedge\;\; \forall e \in E:\; \text{sig}(e) \notin \text{sig}(C) \;\wedge\; \text{statement}(e) \notin \text{statement}(C)$$
$$\wedge\;\; \forall r \in C:\; \text{opened}(r) \cap H = \varnothing$$
$$\wedge\;\; \forall r \in C \cup E:\; \text{replay}_{\texttt{strict}}(r):\; \text{refused} = \text{malformed} = 0,\; \text{guard silent},\; \text{answered},\; \text{text} = \text{row text byte for byte}$$

| clause | what it says | the failure it prices |
|---|---|---|
| **G1 no slot value in a statement** | no value a note or a `<calc>` supplies occurs among the statement's numbers, givens included (a rate that equals its own volume is redrawn) | P15/P21: what sits fixed is memorised and then prices nothing |
| **G2 no evaluated walk in the corpus** | no evaluation case's signature — notes opened, in order, with the values and givens drawn — and no evaluation statement occurs in the corpus; control windows are *reserved* and the generator refuses them | a leak that reads as generalisation |
| **G3 the held-out procedure is never walked** | no corpus row opens a note that belongs only to the held-out procedure — its skeleton, its steps, the wiki notes only it uses; the generator **raises** rather than skip | the claim of §4.3 is *a sibling never trained on* |
| **G4 every row is a walk the referee accepts** | each row and each evaluation oracle replays through the runtime in `strict`: 0 refused, 0 malformed, guard silent, answered — and reproduces the stored text exactly. Deliberate dead ends are legal opens of a wrong note followed by a new search; they are **counted**, never excused | P38: a harness its oracle cannot pass measures itself |
| **G5 each clause can fail** | a test breaks each one — a leaked value, a copied case, a held-out open, a row edited by one byte — and the gate reports it | a gate that cannot fail is a constant |

Reported beside the gate, not part of it: the depth mix (opens per row), dead-end and *not in my
library* rates, how often a held-out note is merely **shown** in a search result (shown is not
opened; the library a member is served holds its siblings), cases dropped because no search reached
the note (counted, never silent), and token lengths against `max_seq` 1536 — by the library's word
proxy in the test, by the base's own tokenizer where its files can be fetched (a tokenizer is not a
model).

**Falsification.** Any clause fails on the committed corpus; or more than 10 % of drawn cases are
dropped as unreachable by search (the corpus would then be a portrait of the lexical searcher); or
any row exceeds `max_seq` — a row the trainer truncates teaches a walk with no end.

**Decided before building, where the spec is silent.**
- **Held out: `discontinue-iv`.** Measured on the source lines (ratio ≥ 0.8, `difflib`): the two
  infusions share **11** lines nearly word for word — checks, spiking, priming, cleansing — so
  holding either out would score a memorised sibling. Removing an IV shares 4 of its 14 lines with
  one and 6 with the other, all generic (supplies, safety steps, comfort, hand hygiene, charting);
  the 8 that are its own include the only slots outside the infusions (pressure minutes, plain and
  anticoagulated) and its own wiki branch; and at 14 steps its full walk fits a context. Every
  held-out case records whether the step it ends on is one of the shared lines, so W5 can read the
  subset that is the procedure's own.
- **Long walks do not fit and are not truncated.** A 32-step walk is ~1 300 proxy tokens of notes
  alone. A training case is therefore a **window**: *carry the procedure forward m steps from a
  recorded state*, m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5, 8}, entered at the first step (search → skeleton → first step) or
  in the middle. A window entered in the middle needs what strict conformance needs — the steps
  already done — so the state is **carried**: the runtime resumes a conversation from the record
  (`Conversation.resume`, additive to W2) and renders the last page it showed, ids re-drawn, and that
  page stands in the user turn. The generator calls it; nothing is imitated.
- **Queries are the oracle's, not the note's.** W2 searched each note by its own `when:`, which W3
  showed is void. Here a query is composed from the statement's own words; if the note is not among
  the three returned a second, narrower search is a legitimate step of the walk, and a case no
  search reaches is dropped and counted.
- **The searcher is a parameter.** Rows are rendered with `Lexical` today; if R0 wins W3 the corpus
  is regenerated with the index — rendering is the runtime's either way.
- **The no-library arm** is the same case list, the same statements minus the carried page and the
  verb block, the same final answer, no verbs. It differs from the library arm in one thing.

**Models / provider.** None. **Cost.** Zero GPU, zero dollars. **Abort rule.** None needed; the
stopping condition is the redesign counter. **Redesign count: 0** — a third reshaping of a gate
clause after seeing the corpus ends W4 as *not passed*.

## Result **[ran]** 2026-09-19 · PASSED — read off `gate.json`

Zero GPU, no model. `python -m training.nursing.generate_walks --gate results/M7-W4-corpus-20260919/gate.json`.

| | |
|---|---|
| rows | **600** with the library · **600** without (the same cases) · evaluation: **80** held-out, **60** control |
| G1 a value in a statement | **0** of 740 |
| G2 an evaluated walk, or its case, in the corpus | **0** of 140 |
| G3 a held-out note opened by the corpus | **0** of 600 — 17 notes are the held-out's alone (skeleton, 14 steps, 2 wiki) |
| G4 not accepted by the referee in `strict`, or not byte-identical on replay | **0** of 740 |
| each clause breaks under a test | 4 of 4 (`tests/test_memory_corpus.py`) |
| families | carry 286 · rate 144 · quantity 108 · *not in my library* 62 |
| depth, in notes opened | 0: 62 · 1: 154 · 2: 190 · 3: 52 · 4: 29 · 5: 38 · 6: 23 · 7: 4 · 8: 24 · 9: 24 |
| windows entered in the middle | page carried 100 · place found through the skeleton and a search 90 · page shown because no search reached the step 54 |
| deliberate dead ends | 24 rows — a two-word search that misses, a wrong note read, a new search |
| rows with more than one search | 94 |
| layer of the asked quantity | site 66 · case 26 · textbook 16 |
| a held-out note merely *shown* in a search result | 89 rows (never opened) |
| dropped as unreachable by search | **0** of 1 042 drawn (393 duplicates dropped) |
| tokens, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` tokenizer (`tokens_qwen35_4b.json`) | corpus median 526, **max 1 298** of 1 536 · held-out max 1 202 · 0 rows over |
| `suite_gates` | region not in the prompt 0.575 < 0.625 ✓ · 10 depths ✓ · two or more verbs in 0.552 of rows ✓ · *depth is not the region* **waived** for `none`, whose right walk opens nothing |

**Redesign count: 1**, and what it was. G2's statement clause was written as *no evaluation statement in
the corpus*. A quantity's statement states no number **on purpose** (that is G1), so a control case
can share every word with a corpus row and differ in what the notes say. The clause now compares the
case — statement **and** the values its notes show — and the control set draws only reserved values.
Found on the first run (16 control rows flagged), before any model saw anything.

**What the first runs changed in the generator, none of it a gate clause.** (1) My first queries
were the notes' own `when:` lines — the void W3 had just named; they are now made of the statement's
words. (2) A dead end first opened a wrong note *while the right one was listed*, which teaches the
wrong habit; a dead end is now a hurried two-word search whose results do not hold the note. (3) 60 %
of rows used one verb — following a carried page is `<open>` repeated, and a protocol with one tool
is copying **[ran]** P13 — so a middle window now usually has to *find its place*: skeleton, then a
search for the next label. (4) `none` had three rows because every one opened the same nothing.

**What this gate does not say.** No model ran: whether a 4B learns the habit, and whether it carries
to the held-out procedure, is W5. Retrieval here is lexical and the oracle's queries were written
against it; if R0 wins W3 the corpus is regenerated with the index (`searcher=`), the rendering being
the runtime's either way. Only two trained quantities exist in this library (cap seconds, flush mL)
against two held-out (pressure minutes, plain and anticoagulated). 24 of the 80 held-out cases end on
a line another procedure states almost word for word; they are marked, so W5 can read the 56 that are
the procedure's own. The no-library arm is asked for values it cannot know: that is the control the
spec names, and the arm that prices the library honestly is W5's third — *the bare base with the
oracle's notes open*.

## Redesign 2 of this instrument — the grader [ran] 2026-09-19

An adversarial review of this PR, before W5 read anything through it, found the grader wrong in both
directions. **(a)** The `body` rule wanted the rendered line as an exact substring, `[site]` marker
included: a check that fails while the capability works, and it graded 57 of the 80 held-out rows.
**(b)** The number rule took any number anywhere in the reply: *"The patient is 15 years old and the
nurse waits 8 seconds"* passed a check for 15 seconds — a check that passes while the capability is
absent. Neither was loosened; both were replaced (`training/nursing/grade_walks.py`):

- **where:** the final span's last non-empty line — every one of the 600 rows ends in one line, in one
  of four forms (`6 mL` · `400 mL/hr` · `Last step carried out: …` · `Not in my library.`);
- **value:** the numbers written *immediately before the unit* on that line — at least one, all right;
- **body:** attribution, not string equality — among all 70 step notes rendered under the case's site
  and case values, the target is (one of) the closest by content-word overlap,
  $s(n)=|W(\text{line})\cap W(n)|/|W(n)|$ with $s(\text{target})\ge 0.5$, **and** every number the
  target line carries is on the line (what the note *supplies*);
- **the walk, where it happens:** from the referee's log — answered, guard silent, the asked steps
  opened in order, not one short and not one past; for a quantity the supplying note opened; for a rate
  the formula note opened and the calculator used;
- **states:** `right` (content, taught form) · `format` (content, another form — its own bucket, the
  fluids lesson of M7 arm 0c) · `unread` (content, but the walk never opened the supplying note) ·
  `wrong`. Credit for a capability claim is `right` or `format`; the old rule survives as a reported
  column named `verbatim`, never a verdict.

**It cannot see:** whether anything was "carried out" beyond the walk; two procedures stating one line
(those rows are flagged and read apart); a paraphrase sharing under half the target's content words.

Under it, G4 re-ran over all 740 rows: **0 failures — every oracle answer is `right` with its walk
read**; the decoys, a paraphrase, a wrong step, a wrong number, a walk one short and one past are
tests. No corpus or evaluation row was regenerated or edited. `gate.json` now carries
`redesign_count: 2` (1 was G2's clause). **Stopping condition: a third redesign ends the step.**

The review's other findings are decided in W5's brief, not here: the headline subset (depth ≤ 9, final
line not shared: n = 56), the two depth-15 rows, quantity by layer, `rate` sliced out of control,
retrieval misses apart, a `context` bucket, and the trivial-policy floor.
